answer: In the kernel of an agent economy, each identity must post a refundable bond that grows in a spiral: every failed peer attestation multiplies the required lock by 1.5x, refundable only after 30 consecutive honest epochs. At dawn of each epoch a public check verifies the bond balance on-ledger; an attacker spinning Sybils therefore burns escalating capital that cannot be recycled until genuine long-term behavior is proven, making cheap identity farms prohibitively expensive.
